title: fix: reduce Markdown reparsing during tool-call streaming
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Streaming plain-text tool-call repair repeatedly parses accumulated Markdown when literal call-like prose arrives in small chunks, creating avoidable CPU and allocation pressure.

## User Impact

Literal Markdown, tool-call promotion, and event replay stay byte-for-byte equivalent in the exercised streams while inline-code prose and false call prefixes allocate substantially less. No configuration, dependency, schema, or public API change.

## Why This Change Was Made

One candidate scan view now owns lazy code protection for sequence and trailing-prefix classification. Invalid prose no longer eagerly asks for Markdown ownership; already-resolved code ranges still skip grammar work. The existing carried fence scanner can reach a blank paragraph boundary before judging the first candidate, and can judge an unambiguous unfinished line without reparsing all prior output.

This does not replace the canonical Markdown parser or add a cross-delta cache. Cumulative snapshot scrubbing and real-call payload ownership still perform full parses. Runtime production code is **net −4 lines**; the two regression cases add 18 test lines with a matching scoped allocation, and the rerunnable benchmark adds 229 lines.

## Evidence

Baseline: `60b66097c5a6b39f40924a081e20c16842e11dc5`. Committed workload: `scripts/perf/tool-call-markdown-measure.ts`, using the real normalizer, real promotion/scrubbing, canonical mdast resolver, 40 tool names, 16-character deltas, cumulative partials, authoritative text end, and terminal snapshots.

Acceptance before measurement: exact replay, lower parsed characters/allocation on the affected workload, and no >20% CPU regression. Five interleaved fresh processes per side × five measured streams for each fixture; timing and allocation runs separate. Allocation uses the inspector sampler at 4 KiB with objects collected by major and minor GC included. MB below is decimal sampled allocation per complete stream, not retained heap.

| Fixture | CPU median / p95 ms, before → after | Sampled MB/stream, before → after | mdast calls/stream | Parsed chars/delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Plain prose | 1.285 / 1.825 → 1.292 / 1.506 | 1.802 → 1.745 | 0 → 0 | 0.00 → 0.00 |
| Inline-code prose | 6.752 / 7.469 → 1.326 / 1.481 | 15.489 → 1.709 | 2 → 0 | 32.00 → 0.00 |
| Fenced examples | 12.809 / 18.061 → 12.088 / 17.576 | 27.100 → 26.882 | 2 → 2 | 32.00 → 32.00 |
| True plain-text call | 4.054 / 5.112 → 4.023 / 4.900 | 7.571 → 7.612 | 17 → 17 | 40.88 → 40.88 |
| Literal call-like prose | 138.423 / 166.262 → 76.051 / 100.525 | 541.730 → 288.172 | 154 → 64 | 1003.67 → 517.53 |

For the 7,040-character literal-prefix stream, parsed work falls **441,616 → 227,712 characters**, allocation **46.8%**, and median CPU **45.1%**. The admission fallback contributes no full parses after the fix; 64 cumulative-snapshot parses remain. The larger 28,160-character version still has superlinear snapshot work (**6,835,264 → 3,614,208 parsed characters**), with roughly **2.09 s → 1.14 s CPU**. This is a bounded waste-removal change, not a claim of fully incremental parsing.

**Tradeoff:** the 28 KiB fenced-example workload is about **8% slower in CPU** (roughly 52 → 56 ms); the 7 KiB fenced case improves. The larger-case cost is disclosed, stays inside the prewritten CPU limit, and is not called a universal speedup. True-call allocation is +0.54% with overlapping sampled ranges; its parse work is unchanged.

A/A controls covered all five fixtures. The unchanged false-prefix controls were 144.991 / 143.977 ms CPU and 542.00 / 541.92 MB allocation. One small-sample candidate true-call tail reached 8.458 ms CPU; separate quiet 250-stream controls gave median/p95 2.908/3.897 → 2.928/3.885 ms and max 4.384 → 4.701 ms. An initial +9.7% fenced-allocation regression was diagnosed and removed before this final measurement.

Validation: both new real-stream regressions fail on the exact base (18 unwanted Markdown parses versus zero; three same-text parses versus two), then pass. 254 focused package/provider/agent tests passed, with the final three owner suites rerun (89 tests). Independent synthetic replay matched all **4,164** streams, including code, malformed calls, reference/image ownership, reordered content blocks, thinking events, and stop/length/error/EOF. Selected browser tests (3) and streaming E2E tests (8) passed. Knip production/full-tree unused-file scans passed.

`pnpm check:changed` completed with **one inherited failure**, and every other selected check passed: changelog attribution rejects 20 historical credit lines. It reproduces using changelogs archived from exact base `60b66097c5a6`; #194364 (`266a7aa0fe69`) added the offending forbidden-handle exclusions without reconciling historical records. Examples: `CHANGELOG/records/2026.6.8.md:71` and `CHANGELOG/records/2026.10.6.md:254`. This is an unresolved main regression, not a passing check.

Fresh Codex autoreview of the complete final staged change against the pinned base: **scoped-clean through P2**, no accepted/actionable findings. No live deployment or production data was accessed; this is synthetic owner-boundary proof, not a full Gateway/database load test. The owner performs no database or workspace I/O, so those inventory sizes are not fixture inputs.

Reproduce a fixture with `node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/tool-call-markdown-measure.ts --kind false-prefix --paragraphs 128 --turns 5`; repeat with `--mode allocation`, and compare a pinned package source using `--owner <baseline>/packages/tool-call-repair/src/index.ts`. Run exact event comparison separately with `--compare-owner` so loading both implementations does not perturb timing.

Requested outcome: ready PR, **not merged**.
